$meta.name: ComponentCondition
$meta.description: Physical condition of a building component.

drift.note: The honest outlier of the five: the VALUES have not diverged. It earns its place because it is declared three times independently, labelled three different ways, and has already been widened once locally — it is the cheapest one to freeze BEFORE it drifts, not after.
drift.api: 4 — Zod enum; the column is a TS union, NOT a DB ENUM (BuildingComponent.ts:103)
drift.localWidening: babel-admin-panel/src/app/(dashboard)/admin/metrics/page.tsx:150 types byCondition over 'good'|'fair'|'poor'|'critical'|'unknown' — a FIFTH value the server can never send. It is a bucket for components with no condition recorded; it belongs in the metrics response type, not here.
drift.labelKeys: THREE label vocabularies for four values: admin `building_components_condition_*`, mobile `building_components_detail_condition_*` AND mobile `task_completion_checklist_condition_*`.
drift.note2: Note there is no `excellent` tier anywhere, despite the name suggesting a 5-point scale. `good` is the top.

companion.note: ComponentStatus (active/replaced/deferred/removed) is declared alongside this one in all three repos and is equally aligned. Not shipped in v1 — it had no measured drift at all, not even a local widening.
